title: Double first cousins
summary: Two brothers marry two sisters: their children are cousins through both parents.
shows: Two brothers (II-1 and II-2) have children with two sisters (II-3 and II-4). Their children (III-1 and III-2) are first cousins through their fathers and again through their mothers, and share all four grandparents.

Double first cousins share on average a quarter of their genes, as half-siblings do. Should they have a child together, its inbreeding coefficient would be 1/8, twice that of a first-cousin union's child.
hard: The two families are joined twice in one generation, which closes a loop: each family's sibship has to sit next to the other's twice over, with both couples' lines kept clear of the other couple's symbols.
